🇺🇸 American officials hint at possible date for US strike on Iran
US President Donald Trump met with his national security team at the White House on Wednesday and Thursday to weigh the possibility of resuming military operations against Iran, senior officials told Fox News on November 6.
Officials also hinted at November 9 as a possible date for an attack, noting that the new moon would leave the Middle East with little to no moonlight, providing favorable conditions for [military operations](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77361).
This appears to contradict Trump's earlier remarks to the Financial Times that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. He added, however, that he would not disclose any attack plans in advance.
Axios reported on November 5 that no decision had yet been made on potential US strikes and that Trump was still weighing his options. Nevertheless, Iraq's prime minister's office tweeted the same day that Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi had told Trump during a phone call that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries.
On November 2, US journalist Tucker Carlson claimed on X that the Trump administration could be just days away from launching a nuclear strike [on Iran. He](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77184) identified Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran as a [potential target](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77229).

🗣🇮🇱 Eisenkot signals he is on track to form a new Israeli government and oust Netanyahu
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar! Party announced on November 6 that he intended to invite all parliamentary factions to join a national emergency government under his leadership.
The Israeli politician said he had made significant progress in coalition talks and achieved breakthroughs, expressing hope of receiving the presidential mandate to form a government early next week.
Eisenkot specifically warned against delaying or obstructing the government’s formation for personal reasons. «They will not be forgiven,» he said.
His bloc has so far secured 21 more recommendations than Benjamin Netanyahu, whose Likud-led camp received 46. The bloc includes Yashar!, B’Yachad, the Democrats, and Yisrael Beytenu.
Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman said he was ready to make painful compromises to end Netanyahu’s rule and avoid new elections. However, he reiterated that his bloc would oppose any government dependent on the Joint List and Ra’am abstaining.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog signaled that he would task a candidate with forming Israel’s next government on November 8.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇮🇱 Israeli intelligence firm warns Iranian vessels may be mapping undersea cables
At least four Iran-linked vessels have been spotted taking unusual routes and loitering near undersea communications cables in the Gulf of Oman in recent weeks, the Financial Times reports.
Israeli maritime intelligence company Windward said three of the vessels are US-sanctioned oil tankers, while the fourth is a small Iranian fishing boat.
🔊"They sailed normally until they reached a specific cable corridor and only then slowed, looped, turned back, loitered, or went dark," Windward told the publication.
🔴 A fishing vessel reportedly lingered over the Europe-India Gateway and Transworld cables
🔴 Three tankers slowed over several cable routes, including 2Africa, which connects Gulf countries to Africa via the Red Sea
🔴 The vessels also allegedly operated above the Falcon cable, which connects Gulf countries to India and Africa
Windward claims the vessels' behavior "fits the profile of mapping the cable routes or placing charges or mines on them while dark."
Iran has repeatedly warned it could target undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz in response to heightened aggression against the Islamic Republic. The first warning [came in April](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68935), with the latest issued in late October, when Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran had detailed plans to attack the cables and block repairs, prolonging internet disruptions if the US and Israel renew their [war against Iran](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76684).[
](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76684)
🔴 At least seven undersea cables cross the Strait of Hormuz, carrying internet traffic and financial and commercial data [between countries](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69879) 
🔴 Satellites are no substitute: they offer less capacity, higher latency, and higher costs, WANA said in an October report
🔴 Tech giants including Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta rely on these cables to connect local networks to global infrastructure
🔴 Disruptions could hit connectivity across the Middle East, Europe, and Asia, as well as cloud services such as Microsoft Azure and [Amazon Web Services](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72522).

events.text:
⚔️ 🇸🇦 Houthis ramp up assault on Saudi-backed forces and infrastructure
 
Yemen’s Ansar Allah has released new combat footage of operations against the enemy in the Kahbub Mountain Range east of the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The footage shows attacks on enemy vehicles, from Toyota pickups to heavily-armored US-made Oshkosh and BATT UMG MRAPs and Jordanian-made Al-Wahsh APCs, firefights with troops, and the use of man-portable anti-tank weapons.
Friday’s release included a 45 second preview, plus a 35-minute video showing fighters scaling mountains, ambushing armored convoys in narrow mountain passes, and fighting in rocky desert areas. The footage provides hints on how the region’s difficult geography helps nullify Saudi Arabia’s overwhelming technological, financial and air power advantage.
Separately on Friday, social media footage showed a large black plume of smoke rising over an unidentified industrial site somewhere in Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi-led coalition reported that it intercepted drones over Mecca and Medina, and two missiles over Najran province. Ansar Allah has repeatedly denied targeting the Islamic holy cities, accusing Riyadh of trying to spark a [religious war](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76337).
Separately, Houthi-aligned Yemeni Armed Forces spokesman Yahya Saree said a Saudi F-15 carried out three airstrikes on the Al-Hadara Market in Taiz governorate’s Al-Waziiyah district, resulting in “dozens of civilian casualties – both killed and wounded.” These “brutal crimes will not go unanswered or unpunished,” he warned.
